To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the learning capacity of health and social care professionals is a key determinant of the success of integrated care initiatives, 2) the learning capacity can be developed through a learning process based on the principles of self-determination theory and 3) this learning process is enhanced by the use of a specific tool, the Learning to Learn (L2L) tool.

(1) the capacity to learn is shaped by individual, social and organizational factors; (2) the ability to learn is a prerequisite for learning to learn; (3) learning to learn requires the ability to reflect on and transform learning processes; and (4) a learning organization is one that is characterized by the capacity to learn to learn.
The capacity to learn how and when to learn is the most important factor that determines the success or failure of integrated care initiatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how learning processes can support and improve integrated care delivery.
the question: how can we foster learning to learn for improved integration of care?
how learning processes can be enhanced to improve integrated care delivery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capacity to self-organize, learn and innovate are the most important conditions that can be fostered in order to improve integrated care delivery.
the capacity to self-learn and learn to self-learn is a necessary condition for the development of integrated care systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to learn how to collaborate, learn from each other, and learn together is essential to achieving effective integration.
learning is not only an important outcome of integrated care, but also a key driver of integrated care.
the capacity to self-organize and to learn how to self-organise is a key factor to the success of integrated care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning is a key enabler of effective integration.
learning to learn is a prerequisite for effective integration and improved health outcomes.
learning to learn can help health and social care organizations to better understand and respond to the challenges of integrated care delivery.
